data.name: Bartholomaeus
data.gender_notes: Bartholomaeus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Bartholomaeus is derived from the Greek and Aramaic words 'Bar-Tholomaios', which can be translated as 'son of Talmai'. It is also believed to mean 'son of Ptolemy'. This name is mentioned in the New Testament as one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. The name Bartholomaeus carries the meaning “Son of Talmai” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Bartholomaeus usually hope their child will grow to embody son of talmai and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bartholomaeus is a name of deep spiritual significance for Christians. It is a reminder of the apostle's unwavering faith and devotion to Jesus. It is also a symbol of the journey of spiritual growth and the pursuit of enlightenment.
data.etymology: Bartholomaeus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Talmai.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bartholomaeus total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: ברתולומיאוס
in_hebrew.meaning: בן תלמי, פירוש השם הוא בן תלמי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ברתולומיאוס הוא שילוב של שני מילים עבריות: 'בן' ו'תלמי'. תלמי הוא שם פרטי עברי שפירושו 'לחרשות', ומכאן שברתולומיאוס פירושו בן של תלמי, או מי שמקורו ממשפחת תלמי. השם מוזכר בברית החדשה כבנו של תלמי, אחד מתלמידי ישו.

in_greek.name: Βαρθολομαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Βαρθολομαῖος προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν Εβραϊκὴ γλώσσα καὶ σημαίνει υἱὸς τοῦ Θαλμαι. Ὁ Θαλμαι εἶναι ἕνα Εβραϊκὸ ὄνομα ποὺ σημαίνει 'ἀρόω', καὶ ἡ λέξη Βαρθολομαῖος ἀποτελεῖται ἀπὸ δύο λέξεις: 'בַּר' (בֵּן) ποὺ σημαίνει 'υἱὸς' καὶ 'Θαλμαι' ποὺ εἶναι τὸ Εβραϊκὸ ὄνομα. Ὁ Βαρθολομαῖος ἦταν ἕνας τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

in_latin.name: Bartholomaeus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Bartholomaeus derivatur ex lingua Hebraea et significat filium Thalmaei. Bartholomaeus fuit unus ex duodecim apostolis Iesu Christi, cuius nomen in Evangelio secundum Matthaeum, Marcum, Lucam et Ioannem commemoratur. Nomen eius in variis formis per Europam diffunditur.

in_english.name: Bartholomaeus
in_english.meaning: Son of Thalmei, a biblical name
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bartholomaeus originates from the Hebrew language, meaning 'son of Thalmei'. It is a significant name in Christian tradition, as Bartholomaeus was one of Jesus Christ's twelve apostles. The name is mentioned in the New Testament in the Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Throughout history, the name has been adapted into various forms across European cultures, maintaining its biblical and spiritual significance.

data.cultural_impact: Bartholomaeus is a Christian name with strong historical roots. It is mentioned in the New Testament in the list of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus. The name has been popular in Europe since the middle ages, particularly in Germany and Scandinavia. In medieval Europe, Bartholomew was regarded as the patron saint of butlers, farm laborers, tanners, and travelers. He was also known as the "patron of constant improvement", symbolizing the hard work and dedication required for personal and professional growth.
data.spiritual_significance: Bartholomaeus is a name deeply rooted in the Christian faith. It is a reminder of the apostle's unwavering commitment to Christ and his mission. The name carries a spiritual significance that inspires faith, dedication, and perseverance. Bartholomaeus is also associated with the process of purification and the transformation of one's self through faith and hard work. In the Catholic tradition, Bartholomew is venerated as a martyr, having been flayed alive for his faith before being decapitated. His life and martyrdom serve as an reminder of the ultimate sacrifices one can make for their beliefs.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bartholomaeus, meaning "son of Talmai" in Aramaic, symbolizes the deep-rooted connection between faith and one's earthly origins. Spiritually, it represents the journey of an individual who, like St. Bartholomew, leaves behind worldly attachments to fully embrace the divine call.
